flstockpile

Read the stock assessment results submitted to ICES: the observed data and the model estimates for each stock, by age and year.

The dataset is published as a set of parquet files in the releases of this repository. This package reads them into plain data frames, and can convert a stock to an FLStock object if the FLCore package is installed. The parquet files can also be read directly, with any parquet reader, in any language.

The current data release is a test release. The content and layout may change.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ices-tools-prod/flstockpile")

Usage

Say where the dataset is. This is the latest data release:

library(flstockpile)

options(flstockpile.url = "https://github.com/ices-tools-prod/flstockpile/releases/latest/download")

A release that will not change is at the same address with its tag, for example .../releases/download/v2026.002.

List the stock assessments. Each one is a stock code and an assessment year, and by default the latest version of each is returned:

stocks <- stockpile_stocks()
nrow(stocks)
#> [1] 47
head(stocks[c("stock_code", "assessment_year", "version", "case_id", "observed", "estimated")])
#>      stock_code assessment_year version          case_id observed estimated
#> 1  ank.27.78abd            2026       1 CAS-88100-V7W8S9    FALSE      TRUE
#> 2   ank.27.8c9a            2026       1 CAS-88489-K0L3G2    FALSE      TRUE
#> 3 bll.27.3a47de            2026       1 CAS-87856-K4Q1M7    FALSE      TRUE
#> 4     caa.27.5a            2026       1 CAS-88823-L1B9G4    FALSE      TRUE
#> 5  cod.21.1.isc            2026       1 CAS-88393-C4D5T8     TRUE     FALSE
#> 6  cod.21.1.osc            2026       1 CAS-88389-H4P0R9     TRUE     FALSE

Get the values for a stock, here the total catch in the last two years. The observed catch and the catch estimated by the model are both stored:

catch <- stockpile_values("sol.27.7d", slot = "catch")
catch <- catch[catch$year >= 2024, c("stock_code", "slot", "type", "year", "value")]
catch[order(catch$year, catch$type), ]
#>    stock_code  slot      type year    value
#> 87  sol.27.7d catch estimated 2024 1374.940
#> 43  sol.27.7d catch  observed 2024 1574.047
#> 88  sol.27.7d catch estimated 2025 1276.954
#> 44  sol.27.7d catch  observed 2025 1251.492

Get the estimates as an FLStock, which needs FLCore (install.packages("FLCore", repos = "https://flr.r-universe.dev")):

library(FLCore)

stock <- stockpile_flstock("sol.27.7d")
summary(stock)
#> An object of class "FLStock"
#> 
#> Name:  
#> Description: FLStock created from SAM model fit 
#> Quant: age 
#> Dims:  age   year    unit    season  area    iter
#>  11  44  1   1   1   1   
#> 
#> Range:  min  max pgroup  minyear maxyear minfbar maxfbar 
#>  1   11  11  1982    2025    3   7   
#> 
#> Metrics: 
#>   rec: 9491 - 49819  (1000) 
#>   ssb: 8875 - 18668  (t) 
#>   catch: 1277 - 6416  (NA) 
#>   fbar: 0.20 - 0.53  (f)

and the observed data with stockpile_flstock("sol.27.7d", type = "observed").

Versions

Submissions made under the same ICES case number form one stock assessment. If a corrected submission arrives, it becomes a new version, and the earlier versions are kept:

stockpile_stocks("meg.27.7b-k8abd", version = "all")[c("stock_code", "version", "latest", "submitted", "n_iters")]
#>        stock_code version latest           submitted n_iters
#> 1 meg.27.7b-k8abd       1  FALSE 2026-05-11 09:43:38       1
#> 2 meg.27.7b-k8abd       2  FALSE 2026-05-11 10:31:59       1
#> 3 meg.27.7b-k8abd       3   TRUE 2026-10-04 13:56:04    1000

Every function takes a version, and an as_of date to see the data as it stood on that date:

stockpile_stocks("meg.27.7b-k8abd", as_of = "2026-06-01")[c("stock_code", "version", "submitted")]
#>        stock_code version           submitted
#> 1 meg.27.7b-k8abd       2 2026-05-11 10:31:59

The tables

The dataset is four parquet files. All of them have the columns stock_code, assessment_year and version, which together identify a version of a stock assessment.

File One row per Read with
stocks.parquet version stockpile_stocks()
sources.parquet submitted object a version was made from stockpile_sources()
values.parquet value stockpile_values()
indices.parquet survey index value stockpile_indices()

stocks has latest (is this the most recent version?), case_id, the stock_key and expert_group of the stock in the ICES Stock Database, the assessment_key of the published assessment in the ICES Stock Assessment Graphs database, submitted, whether the version has observed data and estimated values, the number of survey indices, and the name, desc, ranges (min_age, max_age, plusgroup, min_year, max_year, min_fbar, max_fbar) and dimensions (n_units, n_seasons, n_areas, n_iters) of the stock.

sources has the type (observed or estimated) and class of each submitted object, the submission_id and submitted time of the submission it came from, the file and object name, the submitter’s notes, and the same name, description, ranges and dimensions as in stocks, for that object. units_assumed says whether any numbers or weights were submitted with no units, in which case they are taken to be in thousands and kg.

values has

Column Contents
slot the quantity, named as in an FLStock: catch, catch.n, catch.wt, discards, discards.n, discards.wt, landings, landings.n, landings.wt, stock, stock.n, stock.wt, m, mat, harvest, harvest.spwn, m.spwn
type observed or estimated, or both where the observed and estimated objects have the same values for the slot, which are then stored once
age the age, or missing for a total over ages
year, unit, season, area the year, and the unit, season and area as named by the submitter
value the value; missing values are not stored
units the units of measurement: numbers are always in thousands (1000) and weights in kg; the units of the other slots are those given by the submitter

Where a submitted object had iterations, the values are the medians over the iterations.

indices has the same columns as values, with the name of the index, slots named as in an FLIndex (index, catch.n, effort, …), and the part of the year the survey covers (startf, endf).

A list of FLStock objects made from the same tables, flstocks.rds, is published with each release.

How the data are made

The scripts that make the tables from the submissions are in data-raw: get_submissions.R downloads the submitted files, make_parquet.R makes the tables, and check_parquet.R checks them against the submitted objects. object_types.csv records which submitted objects hold observed data and which hold model estimates.
